body: claimed: main session (agent: island late returns) · 2026-11-07T03:18Z · worktree on dd8bc95 · plan: the round-6 next step - a lead-scoped dependency (only the pieces the ramp high() takes) or a corner landing off the lead, so the island's SW-corner piece returns legally and the ring fallback lifts.

Cause/plan (agent on dd8bc95): the round-6 finding stands - the SW-corner piece of every lap is refused by `high()`/`late` because its lead holds stock right to its end. Plan per the issue: (a) a lead-scoped dependency in `lift_split::depends` (read only the stretch of lead `high()` would ramp along on the spiral's stock), then (b) a corner landing off the lead (a disc-clear point within a few RAMP_RUN of the piece, descended as a chord). Note first: on dd8bc95 the island never reaches the lift at all - it is refused by the issue #13 growth budget (31,090 r of growth work vs `WORK_MAX` 30,000 r, "ran past its planning budget after 163 revolutions"); the readings below lift that budget locally to reach the hop law.

Final (agent): neither attempt holds; the fallback is kept, nothing landed (worktree clean on dd8bc95). Readings (release, `hsm_one` island, `WORK_MAX` raised locally to reach the lift):

- **Baseline**: hops 9 (cap 8), highs 4, rides 1; the 9 hops are pieces 197..237 step 4 at (5.47, 7.89), leads 24.7-24.9 mm.
- **(a) lead-scoped dependency** (`ramp_reads`: per piece, the lead stretch to the first disc-clear point >= RAMP_RUN back, on the stock as the spiral leaves it; `depends` reads max(that, LEAD_READ)): hops still 9, highs 4 -> 8. Those corner pieces read only 1.1 mm on the spiral's stock (<= LEAD_READ), so their dependencies never change. The stock under their leads is not a missing dependency: it is the sub-bite slivers (20 deg ~ 0.30 mm on r5) the spiral's floor rides shaved lap after lap. The re-order lifts over those leads, so the slivers pile up on the west wall.
- **(b) corner landing** (`LinkLaw::corner`: 24 directions x {1, 1.5, 2.2, 3} RAMP_RUN round the piece's first point, rapid column disc-clear, chord inside the centre area, peek <= bite, no crossing): no legal point. Every point behind the piece or on the wall side holds stock in the disc. Every disc-clear point (inward, x >= 6.4) reads 28.5-30.5 deg on the chord into the wall slivers (bite 15) and crosses an earlier return. Straight-behind-and-below reads 17.0 deg.
- What it would take: a near-tangent approach (within 4 deg of the piece, so ~13 mm along the wall to clear 0.9 mm sideways), descended over its first RAMP_RUN and then fed at the floor as a cut. That floor stretch would cross the earlier laps' wall runs (they lie between x 5.49 and 6.4), so the crossing law refuses it. Real options: put the slivers back, i.e. ride (floor-cut) the corner pieces' leads when the re-order skips them, so the lap keeps the spiral's shaving; or re-calibrate the budget together with that ride.
- Separately, the issue #13 growth budget refuses the island first (31,090 r vs 30,000 r). Even if the hop law is solved, the island also needs `WORK_MAX` raised (~5 %+), with its own calibration.

Claim released by the main session after round 7 (no code landed; readings in the comment above). Next attempt should start from the agent's proposed approach: keep cutting along the corner pieces' leads at the floor in the re-ordered plan (so each lap still shaves the west-wall slivers as the spiral did), then recalibrate the #13 growth budget for the island (it now refuses it first at 31,090 vs 30,000 tool radii).

claimed: main session (Opus 5.5, issue loop) · 2026-11-07T08:30Z · worktree agent-issue7 · plan: round 8 - floor-ride the corner pieces' leads the re-order skips (keep the spiral's west-wall shaving), then recalibrate the #13 growth budget for the island

Round 8 (no code landed; docs in db95014, patch held at tmp/issue7-r8-lead-ride.patch incl. a WORK_MAX 40,000 probe; lift.rs would reach 427 lines, split before landing).

LinkLaw::ride_lead (after `late` in lift::schedule): a skipped corner piece whose lead holds stock to its first point is cut from a point stepped back 0-18 mm along the walk's own vertices (resampled points crossed at (6.67, 34.60)); ridden stretches read 17-31 deg (bound 47.5).

Readings (release, hsm_one island): hops 9 -> 2 (cap 8), highs 4 -> 30, rides 1 -> 9, 6 leads ridden; air 2,912 + lift 6,429 vs 8,221 cut = 1.14x (budget 1.5x); 61,848 moves, rest 3.5 mm2; verifier silent.

Not landed because the island plan then fails three acceptance laws the ring fallback skipped, all around the island's NE corner (41-47, 26-34) in the spiral's own growth, not at the ridden leads: 176 in-cut turns past 5 deg (worst 80.2), 6 descents into stock for 2 levels (law allows 2), worst load 125 deg / 79.4% D at (43.66, 25.81) - the spiral alone already reads 125 deg there.

Next, in order: (1) the spiral's growth near the island's NE corner (load + turns); (2) account the extra descents (the 2 hops, and whether retract-plane return descents count as descents into stock); (3) then land ride_lead with WORK_MAX ~32,000 r and re-time the #13 band refusal. Claim released.

claimed: main session (agent: issue-7 round 9) · 2026-11-08T09:59Z · worktree .claude/worktrees/issue-7 / branch issue/7-island-late-returns · plan: round 9 - start from tmp/issue7-r8-lead-ride.patch (ride_lead), attack the NE-corner growth load/turn laws and the descent accounting, then recalibrate WORK_MAX

Round 9 (agent, on origin/main 0015347): no code landed. Held work is pushed to branch `issue/7-island-late-returns` (44649f1 = the round-8 `ride_lead` patch re-applied, fdf86eb = a column-feed probe), `Refs #7`, no PR.

Readings (release, `HSM_ONE=island hsm_one`):

- **main as is**: the #13 growth budget still refuses the island first ("ran past its planning budget after 163 revolutions"), and the Offset rings cut it. Verifier silent.
- **round-8 patch** (`ride_lead` + `WORK_MAX` 40,000), same numbers as round 8: hops 2, highs 30, rides 9, leads 6; air 2,912 + lift 6,429 vs 8,221 cut = 1.14x (budget 1.5x); 61,848 moves; rest 3.51 mm2; load 125 deg / 79.4 % D at (43.66, 25.81); 176 breaks past 5 deg (worst 80.2); descents 6. **New on this main: the verifier reports 4 `RapidInStock`.** It did not in round 8; the #202/#205 verifier changes now read the whole rapid. All 4 are retract-plane returns (`LinkLaw::high`) rapiding straight down from z 1 to the lift (-4.7) on level 1, at (9.23, 34.68), (8.82, 34.70), (8.97, 34.74) by the north wall and (41.21, 25.22) by the island's NE corner. `high()` takes the column as clear when `stock_clear(p, r)` holds on the planner raster, so a sliver of the walls' margin smaller than a cell gets through.
- **column read one cell wider** (`stock_clear(p, r + ras.h)`): hops 2 -> 9 (cap 8), and the plan falls back to the rings again.
- **column fed from over the material top** (fdf86eb: the rapid stops at the plunge height, or at the hop plane when there is no plunge height, then plunges, as `feed_down` does for the ladder's hops): verifier silent, but descents 6 -> 54. The quality grid sees stock under the disc rim at most of the high() columns, not just at the 4 the verifier flags. The column law is too tight across the board, not at a few corner cases.

What was learned / next, in order:
1. **The island spiral itself is the blocker, ahead of the hops.** Its growth reads 125 deg (79.4 % D) and makes 176 turns over 5 deg round the island's NE corner (41-47, 26-34). That is where the fronts going round the north side turn the island's convex corner down toward the slit (the seed is at (13, 18), the slit runs east at y 18). Until the growth step holds the bound there, the island fails `judge`'s load and break laws whatever the returns do. A corner-specific growth step (a smaller step, or a trochoidal bite on the convex corner) is the next attempt.
2. **Retract-plane returns need a real column law**: either check stock against the measuring tolerance (`r` plus a cell plus the graze), or descend at feed and count it as an accounted descent. Either way it costs hops or descents, which feeds back into the hop cap and the 2-descents law.
3. Only after 1 and 2: land `ride_lead` (split lift.rs, now 427 lines) and recalibrate `WORK_MAX` (the island needs about 31,100 r).

Claim released.
Effort lowered from `effort:max` to `effort:high` on the maintainer's instruction (2026-11-11): this is worked by the high-tier worker.

claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-11T13:55Z · worktree .claude/worktrees/issue-7 / branch issue/7-r10-corner-reading · plan: round 10 - measure first where rounds 6-9 did not: whether the island's NE-corner overload (125 deg, 176 breaks) survives the growth step search's smallest step on current main; if a step-level fix holds the bound, land it, else no code and a close-or-redesign recommendation

Round 10 (issue-worker-high, on origin/main d1920031): no PR. Held work pushed to `issue/7-r10-corner-reading` (e4039ef0, `Refs #7`, not for merge).

**Approach (new vs rounds 6-9):** rounds 6-9 all worked on the returns (late, lead-scoped dependency, corner landing, ride_lead, column feed). Round 9 named the growth load at the NE corner as the real blocker and proposed "a smaller step". This round measured that first: instrumented the growth step search on the island.

Note: main does not compile in `camcraft-motion` right now (#844, trochoid_slot.rs vs `measure()`'s new `Result`). The readings below stub that locally (not pushed).

**Readings** (release, `HSM_ONE=island hsm_one`, `WORK_MAX` lifted locally to reach the growth):
- **The step was never the limit.** At revs 153-159 (NE corner) all 7 tried steps, from 1.88 mm down to 0.088 mm, read the same first exceedance (rev 159: 59.5 deg every time). The fallback then keeps the first one, the LARGEST step, and walks it whole: 125 deg / 79.4 % D at (43.66, 25.81). That is the 125 deg / 176 breaks round 9 reported. The tries stop at the first reading past the bound (`walk_until`), so their "least overload" compares numbers that cannot be compared. Filed as #845 (P1, a defect on every growth plan).
- **With the fallback re-walking each tried step whole** (e4039ef0): every overloaded island revolution reads <= 55 deg (bound ~47.5; the worst is now at the SW wall, (17.58, 6.01)). No NE-corner overload is left.
- **But the growth work doubles:** 61,971 r (round 9: ~31,100; `WORK_MAX` 30,000). Smaller steps mean more revolutions, and every revolution re-walks the whole C-shaped ring round the island. With the budget at 40,000 the plan is refused at 127 revolutions.
- **And the hop law still refuses**: with the budget lifted, "the HSM plan would reach 9 passes a level by retract hops (over 8)". The plan never gets to `judge`. Round 9's other open items still stand: no `ride_lead`, and no column law for retract-plane returns (4 `RapidInStock`).

**Why this round stops:** making the island plan honestly costs about 2x the growth budget on the slit-C spiral. It still needs ride_lead plus a real high-return column law. That is three coupled law changes (#13 budget, hop cap, rapid column) under the safety floor, and each one moves other fixtures. It is not one bounded change at this tier.

**Recommendation for the maintainer:** (a) **close #7 as won't-do**. For island regions, the named Offset-ring fallback is the accepted behaviour: it is visible, named in the notes and verifier-silent. Keep #845 open on its own merits (it also lowers the load of every other growth plan). If islands on the HSM planner are still wanted later, file (b) as a new `needs-research` item, not round 11 of this one: **decompose island regions into island-free cells** (split at the slit and the island's far side, plan each cell's spiral separately, enter each later cell from cleared stock through a link law of its own). That removes the C-ring that makes every revolution re-walk the island, and with it the doubled work and most of the hops. Rough size: a new decomposition module plus an inter-cell link and entry law, verifier coverage and fixture recalibration. Several PRs, `effort:max`.

The effort tier was not the limit here; the issue's scope is. Claim released.
